subject: Startups
title: The SPAC Boom and Bust
description: A short lesson to help you apply The SPAC Boom and Bust.

hook.text: In 2021, more companies went public through SPACs than traditional IPOs. By 2023, most were trading below $2.

buildup.text: Low interest rates and stimulus money fueled a SPAC frenzy. Celebrities like Shaq and A-Rod launched their own SPACs.

discovery.text: SPACs let companies make forward-looking revenue projections that IPOs can't. Many projections were wildly optimistic.

twist.text: Lucid Motors SPAC'd at a $24B valuation. Two years later, it was worth $6B. Clover Health fell 80% post-merger.

climax.text: The SEC sued SPAC sponsors for misleading investors. New rules now require SPAC projections to face IPO-level scrutiny.

punchline.text: Easy money in creates easy money out.

quiz.question: What was a major problem with SPAC mergers?
options: Many made wildly optimistic revenue projections
They took too long to complete
